post_text:
We rejected a dynamic JSON schema for our core payment API and forced strict, statically typed Protobuf contracts instead.

Everyone wanted the flexibility of arbitrary payloads to move faster.

I spent weeks second-guessing myself, wondering if my stubbornness was just slowing down the product launch.

The team complained about the extra compilation step and the rigid schema migration rules we enforced.

I lay awake worrying that I was being an overly dogmatic gatekeeper.

Two years later, a downstream team refactored their database schema and accidentally changed a critical field from an integer to a string.

Our CI pipeline caught the breaking change instantly during the build phase, preventing a silent production catastrophe.

We did not have to spend the weekend debugging corrupted transaction logs.

The quiet safety of a rigid contract is rarely celebrated when things are going well. It only proves its value when the chaos of organizational growth starts breaking unwritten assumptions.

What I learned:

Strict, boring API contracts protect systems from human drift far better than any post-incident postmortem ever can.
